edits.text:
Tuberous sclerosis: the tells Periungual (ungual) fibroma — a firm flesh-colored growth from the nail fold, appearing in adolescence or adulthood · Calcified subependymal nodules — head CT shows them lining the lateral ventricles; cortical tubers are seen better on MRI · A fall explained by a seizure — epilepsy affects most patients, from infantile spasms in infancy to a first seizure at any age, with intellectual disability, autism and behavior disorders · The other skin lesions — ash-leaf (hypopigmented) macules, facial angiofibromas, and the shagreen patch, an orange-peel plaque over the lower back · The other organs — cardiac rhabdomyoma, renal angiomyolipoma, retinal hamartoma; a subependymal nodule can grow into a subependymal giant cell astrocytoma that obstructs CSF flow and needs resection · Diagnosis and surveillance — the clinical constellation or TSC1/TSC2 testing; then skin and eye examinations, serial brain and kidney MRI, baseline echocardiogram with serial ECG, baseline EEG, and neuropsychiatric screening
Tuberous sclerosis vs. the distractors Neurofibromatosis type 1 — also autosomal dominant with seizures, but the skin shows café-au-lait macules and cutaneous neurofibromas on the trunk, and the tumor is an optic glioma; no nail fibromas or calcified periventricular nodules · Von Hippel-Lindau — cerebellar and retinal hemangioblastomas; no skin hamartomas · Ataxia-telangiectasia — autosomal recessive; ataxia from early childhood, abnormal eye movements, telangiectasias of the eyes and skin · Infective endocarditis — fever, dyspnea and a murmur; its nail finding is a splinter hemorrhage under the nail plate, not a fibroma
edits.why: Q5 teaching: the tells, organ findings, SEGA complication, surveillance, and why each original distractor fails.

items.stem: 17-year-old boy found confused at the bottom of a staircase after an unwitnessed fall, with a forehead contusion, a firm fibroma growing from under a toenail, and calcified nodules along the lateral ventricles on head CT
items.companion: Nail fibroma plus calcified subependymal nodules; the fall was likely a seizure

items.stem: 5-month-old with clusters of flexion spasms, three oval hypopigmented macules on the trunk, and an intracardiac mass on echocardiography
items.companion: Infantile spasms, ash-leaf macules and a cardiac rhabdomyoma

items.stem: 14-year-old with tuberous sclerosis who has two weeks of morning headaches and vomiting; MRI shows an enlarging mass near the foramen of Monro with dilated lateral ventricles
items.companion: A subependymal nodule that grew and obstructed CSF flow; resection

items.stem: 6-year-old with facial angiofibromas, hypopigmented macules, epilepsy and cortical tubers on MRI, newly diagnosed with tuberous sclerosis complex
items.key: Serial brain and kidney MRI with baseline echocardiography
items.companion: Surveillance follows the organs: brain, kidney, heart, plus skin, eye, EEG and neuropsychiatric screening
items.d1: Plasma metanephrines with annual dilated retinal examination
items.d2: Serum calcitonin with annual thyroid ultrasonography
